wrapup.desc: When this agent ends because of a timeout or exhausted step budget, the system injects this wrap-up prompt to run a final round. taskTimeout.desc: Task-timeout wrap-up (a separate set from the per-run wrap-up above): injected when the entire task reaches its timeout limit and is about to end. Its meaning often differs from per-run wrap-up. For example, the planner's per-run prompt says “keep planning without stopping,” while its task-timeout prompt says “stop on time and make the final assessment.” Leave blank to use the built-in default.

triggers.desc: Triggers run this custom agent automatically. Each activation creates and runs a new session (visible on the Chat page). You can select multiple conditions. The system automatically appends the trigger reason and relevant task/finding/goal to your base message.
triggers.policyLabel: Trigger processing policy (controls queuing and merging)
triggers.policyParallel: Parallel: each trigger immediately opens its own session and runs concurrently, without merging. Triggers beyond the concurrency limit are queued until a slot is available.
triggers.policyByTask: Serial, merge by task: only one run of this agent executes at a time. Queued event triggers for the same task are merged into one session.
triggers.policyAll: Serial, merge all: only one run of this agent executes at a time. When processing the queue, all pending triggers are merged into one session.
triggers.policyNone: Serial, no merging: only one run of this agent executes at a time. Each trigger opens its own session.

trafficCapture.title: Traffic capture
trafficCapture.desc:
When enabled, all agents’ HTTP traffic passes through the recording proxy and is stored. Agents receive traffic_search / traffic_get tools and proxy settings, with proxy instructions in their prompts.

When disabled (default), no traffic is recorded. Agents do not receive proxy settings or traffic tools, and their prompts contain no proxy instructions. Switching takes effect immediately by recreating agents.
trafficCapture.on: On · Recording traffic and injecting proxy settings
trafficCapture.off: Off · No recording or proxy injection

agentBinding.title: Automatic agent traffic linking
agentBinding.desc:
Off by default. When enabled, the report agent triggered by a new finding checks existing HTTP requests and responses, links matching traffic, then writes the report. Inspecting packets and making extra tool calls increases token usage.

Reporting still works for TCP, uncaptured packets, or unmatched traffic. This setting does not affect traffic capture, manual linking, or access to saved evidence. Applies from the next agent cycle; disabling immediately rejects new automatic links.

globalProxy.title: Global proxy
globalProxy.desc:
All agents’ target traffic exits through this proxy to mask the source IP or use a relay. Supports http / https / socks5 and user:pass authentication. Leave blank for direct connections.

With traffic capture enabled, this proxy is upstream of the recording proxy, so traffic is still recorded before forwarding. With capture disabled, proxy settings are injected directly into agents’ Bash / WebFetch execution. This is independent of the web search and LLM proxies.

Note: with capture disabled, socks5 depends on each command-line tool supporting ALL_PROXY. curl supports it, but some tools may ignore it. Enabling traffic capture is recommended for socks5: the MITM proxy establishes the connection itself, without relying on tool support.
globalProxy.placeholder: socks5://user:pass@host:1080 or http://host:port (blank for direct connection)
globalProxy.configured: Configured · All target traffic uses this proxy
globalProxy.notConfigured: Not configured · Target traffic connects directly

constraints.title: Behavior constraint injection
constraints.desc:
When enabled, each task’s behavior constraints—the allow/deny entries managed in its overview—are appended to agent system prompts to restrict exploration, such as “test only the current port” or “no brute force”.

Injection is controlled separately for the planner and worker, both enabled by default. Changes apply on the next cycle without recreating agents. When disabled, that agent no longer receives these constraints.

experimental.title: Experimental features
experimental.desc:
These features are still being validated and are off by default. They may change agent behavior or affect stability; understand their impact before enabling them.

noa context compression: a model compresses long conversation histories (norma v0.4.0). When enabled, all four connected agent types (planner / worker / main agent / chat) use noa instead of built-in compression. The source material is retained in the task’s working directory for review. Changes apply to subsequent runs without recreating agents. Disabling immediately restores built-in compression.

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.desc:
The web search master switch and source settings. Enable it before allowing web_search in individual agent settings. Search returns titles, links, and summaries; WebFetch retrieves page contents. Search bypasses the recording proxy and is independent of traffic capture.

Choose DuckDuckGo (ddgs) (no key), Brave (free tier) (Brave API Key required), Tavily (Tavily API Key required), or DeepSeek (reuses the current LLM configuration). With the master switch off, agents cannot enable web search.
webSearch.on: Master switch on · Enable search separately for each agent
webSearch.off: Off · Agents cannot enable web search
webSearch.deepseekDesc1: This source reuses the currently active LLM configuration. It therefore supports only official DeepSeek models, and the configuration must use the anthropic protocol. DeepSeek’s OpenAI protocol endpoint does not support server-side search. Changing the LLM configuration may stop this source from working.
webSearch.deepseekDesc2: Unlike other sources, DeepSeek’s servers perform the search. Each search makes an additional model call and incurs token costs. Search requests do not use the outbound proxy above and are not recorded as traffic. Results include titles and links only, without summaries. WebFetch retrieves page contents if needed.
webSearch.deepseekDesc3: You must check these requirements yourself; the system does not enforce them. Use “Test search” below to verify with an actual request.

pool.title: LLM rotation · Failover
pool.desc: When enabled, agents without an explicitly assigned model automatically switch to the next configuration if the current one is unavailable due to insufficient balance, expired keys, rate limits, or service errors.

enable.label: Enable rotation
enable.hint: Off by default. When disabled, only the active configuration is used, and failures are returned directly.

bindFallback.label: Allow fallback for explicitly assigned models
bindFallback.hint: Off by default: when an agent or task specifies a configuration, only that configuration is used and failures are returned directly, without silently changing models. When enabled, a failed assigned configuration falls back to the rotation chain below.

order.label: Rotation order
order.tooFew: Available configurations: {n}. Rotation requires at least two participating configurations with API Keys.

recoverNow.title: Recover now: close the circuit and retry this configuration on the next call

pool.note: The active configuration is always first; others follow in descending priority order, set individually. Failed configurations enter cooldown (60s → 5min → 30min) and are skipped until recovery. Configurations whose context windows cannot fit the current request are skipped. Agents and tasks with explicitly assigned models do not participate by default.

profile.descNew: New configurations are not activated automatically. Click “Set as active” on the card to use one.
profile.descEdit: Click Save after editing. Saving the active configuration applies changes to all agents immediately.

model.label: Model
model.loadTitle: Load available models from the API

proxy.label: Proxy (optional)
proxy.hint: Only outbound LLM requests use this proxy. Supports http/https/socks5 with optional credentials, e.g. socks5://user:pass@host:port. URL-encode special characters in passwords. Leave blank for direct connections.

sessionHeader.label: Custom session header (optional)
sessionHeader.hint: If a header name is provided, every request includes it with the current session ID as its value, such as conv-12 for chat or exp3-worker-i87 for a worker. Intended for gateways using session headers for prompt caching or sticky routing. The value stays stable across turns within a session and differs between sessions. Leave blank to omit.

profile.rateHint: Rate limit 0 means unlimited; limits are shared by all agents. Context window is in K (thousands of tokens): 0 uses the 200K default, and the maximum is 1000 (1M). Setting it too high may prevent compression from triggering.

priority.label: Rotation priority
priority.hint: Higher numbers are selected first. The active configuration is always first regardless of priority. Configurations with equal priority alternate positions to share quota.

exclude.label: Exclude from rotation
exclude.hint: When enabled, this configuration is excluded from failover but remains available to agents or tasks that explicitly select it. Useful for expensive configurations reserved for specific agents.

streaming.label: Streaming output · streaming
streaming.hint: Enabled by default. SSE streaming provides live progress and token counts. Disabling uses true non-streaming mode (stream:false), returning the complete response at once. This can bypass faulty gateway SSE implementations, such as empty frames or missing reasoning fields, but removes live progress updates.

maxTokens.label: Output limit · max tokens
maxTokens.hint: Maximum tokens generated in one response, sent with each request. 0 (default) omits this field and uses the server default. This differs from the context window above, which represents total model capacity and is used locally only to calculate compression thresholds. A limit that is too low may truncate a reasoning model during reasoning before it produces an answer.

maxTokensFieldHint.openai: Selects the key used to send the limit. max_tokens is the default and is recognized by most compatible gateways. Official OpenAI reasoning models (o series / GPT-5) use max_completion_tokens and reject max_tokens with unsupported_parameter.
maxTokensFieldHint.anthropic: Selectable only for the openai format. Anthropic always uses max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.openai-responses: Selectable only for the openai format. The Responses API always uses max_output_tokens.

thinkingType.label: Thinking switch · thinking.type
thinkingType.hint: Controls whether to send the thinking field. Omit leaves it out for compatibility with models such as MiniMax; Off sends disabled; On sends enabled. Independent of the effort level below.

effort.label: Reasoning effort · reasoning_effort
effort.hint: An independent effort level (OpenAI reasoning_effort / Anthropic output_config.effort). Some interfaces enable reasoning through effort alone without a thinking field, so effort can be set while omitting the thinking switch.

toast.created: Created: {name} (click “Set as active” on its card to use it)
toast.savedActive: Saved. The active configuration applies immediately without restarting.

connect.title: Connection retry
connect.trigger: Before a connection is established or HTTP 200 is received: network errors such as connection resets, read/write timeouts, and DNS failures, plus HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504.
connect.skips: Other status codes (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 413 / 422, etc.) are definitive rejections and are passed upward immediately because resending would fail again.
connect.desc: Resends the same request unchanged. Once streaming starts after HTTP 200, interruptions are no longer handled by this layer.
connect.offHint: -1 = no retries; pass failures upward immediately

empty.title: Empty response retry
empty.trigger: HTTP 200 with a normal stop finish_reason but no content blocks anywhere in the response. This includes empty gateway frames, frames missing reasoning fields, and transient sampling failures.
empty.skips: Excludes empty responses caused by max_tokens truncation. Increase the output limit instead; resending would hit the same limit.
empty.desc: Resends the full prompt. Long contexts can be expensive, so keep the retry count modest.

stream.title: Same-provider retry before output
stream.trigger: Problems after the stream is established with HTTP 200—connection interruptions, provider overloaded errors, or in-stream 429 / 5xx events—provided no tokens have yet been delivered to the caller.
stream.skips: Does not retry exhausted quota (402 / insufficient_quota, handled by rotation), context overflow (413 / context length, handled by compression), or definitive 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 422 rejections.
stream.desc: Replays the same request with the same configuration. Because no output has been delivered, replay does not duplicate model output or tool execution.
stream.offHint: -1 = pass interrupted streams directly to the outer intent retry layer

breaker.title: Rotation circuit breaker
breaker.where: Application · One global policy per process
breaker.trigger: Opens the circuit when consecutive transient failures (429, 5xx, network errors) reach the threshold. Definitive failures such as insufficient balance (402), expired keys (401 / 403), or missing models (404) open it immediately.
breaker.skips: A successful call resets the count to zero, so occasional failures do not accumulate indefinitely.
breaker.desc: An open circuit enters cooldown, during which rotation skips this configuration. State is stored in the database and survives restarts.
breaker.offHint: -1 = transient failures never open the circuit (definitive failures still do)

intent.title: Intent retry
intent.where: Application · One global policy per process
intent.trigger: When earlier layers cannot recover and a worker ends with model_error: inner retries are exhausted, or the stream fails after output delivery has started, when safe replay is no longer possible and the entire intent must run again.
intent.skips: Quota exhaustion is handled by rotation, so it is not retried here. Paused, terminated, or wrapping-up tasks yield immediately without waiting through backoff.
intent.desc: Reruns the entire intent from the beginning. As the outermost layer, each retry can multiply the attempts made by the inner layers again.
intent.offHint: -1 = no rerun; immediately mark the intent as blocked

override.label: Retry overrides
override.hint: Applies only to this configuration, overriding global defaults from “Retries and backoff”. Leave fields blank to inherit. A retry count of -1 disables that layer; a specified interval uses fixed delays instead of exponential backoff. Circuit breaking and intent retries apply process-wide and can only be adjusted on the global page.

retry.intro: A failed model call passes through five retry layers from inner to outer: <chain>connection → empty response → same-provider retry before output → rotation circuit breaker → intent retry</chain>. Outer layers act only after inner attempts are exhausted, so counts <emph>multiply</emph>. Maximizing every layer can turn one transient problem into dozens of requests. Leaving everything blank preserves the existing defaults. The first three layers can be overridden per model configuration.

toast.saved: Saved and applied immediately (the current in-progress call keeps its previous settings)

notifyPage.subtitle: Send finding notifications to channels such as DingTalk, Feishu, and WeCom. Configure delivery timing and filters separately for each channel.

toast.testSent: Test message sent ({ms} ms). Check the channel.

global.title: Global settings
global.baseUrlHint: Destination for the “View details” button in messages. Leave blank to omit the button.
global.digestHint: Applies only to channels in Digest mode.

sheet.kindLocked: Channel type cannot be changed because doing so would replace its entire credential configuration. Create a new channel instead.
sheet.noFields: This channel’s form has not been defined (missing CHANNEL_FIELDS entry in the frontend). Add the definition and try again.
sheet.modeDigest: Digest · Batch findings into one message per interval
sheet.modeHint: To send high-severity findings immediately and receive periodic digests, create two channels: one real-time with High as the minimum severity, and one digest with no severity limit.
sheet.rateHint: Leave blank for the channel default. 0 means unlimited. Excess messages are delayed, not discarded.

filter.title: Filters (leave blank for no filtering)
filter.includeHint: One keyword per line. Matching is case-insensitive and uses substrings. Leave blank to include all types.
filter.excludeHint: Exclusions take precedence. If both filters match, the finding is excluded.
filter.idsHint: Leave task/asset fields blank for no restriction. If specified, they must overlap with the finding’s tasks/assets.
filter.onStatusChange: Also send when a finding’s remediation status changes (real-time mode only)

masked.savedTail: Saved (ends in {tail}) · Enter a new value to replace it; leave blank to delete this field
masked.saved: Saved · Enter a new value to replace it; leave blank to delete this field

secret.label: Signing secret
secret.help: Enter this when “Signature” is selected in the bot security settings. Leave blank for custom keywords or when security settings are disabled.

secret.label: Signature verification secret
secret.help: Enter this if signature verification is enabled for the bot; otherwise leave blank.

headers.label: Custom request headers
headers.help: One KEY=VALUE per line, e.g. Authorization=Bearer xxx

body_template.label: Request body template
body_template.help: Leave blank for the built-in template. Variables: '{{.Title}} {{.Batch}} {{.Count}} {{.HomeURL}} {{.SentAt}}', plus .Name/.VulnClass/.Severity/.Summary/.Assets/.DetailURL/.StatusLabel under range .Items. Use '{{json .Xxx}}' rather than '{{.Xxx}}' for strings; otherwise, quotation marks in titles can break the JSON.

base_url.label: API address
base_url.help: Leave blank for the official endpoint. Set this for a self-hosted Bot API reverse proxy.

tls.label: Implicit TLS
tls.help: Enable for port 465; disable for 587, which uses STARTTLS automatically.
